question.text: An inverted yield curve, where short-term rates are higher than long-term rates, is generally considered an indicator of:

explanation.text: The Logic: An inverted yield curve — where short-term rates are higher than long-term rates — is generally seen as a signal that the economy may go into a recession. The Trap: A stable rate environment and strong growth would typically produce a normal upward-sloping curve, not an inverted one. Note: Yield-curve shape is one input among many in macro analysis; this question covers only the recession-signal interpretation.
